# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14 (Bi-Vb Pc14)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc14

**Collection:** Vinaya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 14, titled *Dutiyikauyyojana* ("Meeting a man on a street" or dismissing a companion), establishes a rule concerning the conduct of Buddhist nuns when in public spaces. The rule proscribes a nun who, seeking privacy, dismisses her companion nun to stand alone with a man in public thoroughfares, whether on a carriage road, in a cul-de-sac, or at a crossroads, incurring an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the framing narrative, the nun Thullanandā dismisses her companion in order to whisper in a man's ear; modern comparative studies cite this episode as an example within monastic law addressing active female desire and indiscreet encounters [Collett 2014]. The accompanying word commentary (*padabhājanīya*) details the stages of the infraction: dismissing a companion nun with the wish to misbehave entails a *dukkaṭa* offense while leaving the range of sight or hearing, which ripens into a full *pācittiya* once out of sight or hearing [Hüsken 1997]. This injunction forms part of a wider set of rules ensuring that nuns are not left unchaperoned either within or outside settlements [Hüsken 1997].

The rule corresponds to a well-attested disciplinary precept across diverse Buddhist Vinaya lineages, having parallels in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Vibhaṅga recensions of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāsaṅghika, Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravādin, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan. Modern English translations include that of Bhikkhu Brahmali.
